henry.title: Apollo 11: The First Steps on the Moon
henry.intro: Be a history detective about July 1969. (About 15 minutes.)
steps: 📖 Read each chunk below. Tap 🔊 if you want.
🗓️ Find launch and splashdown dates on the NASA page.
links: Look at the top box: find the 3 astronauts and the launch and splashdown dates.
NASA photo: a bootprint on the Moon
Look at the photo. Why is it still there?

passage.text: 🎯 In 1961, President Kennedy set a big goal. Land people on the Moon and bring them home safely.
passage.a: Land people on the Moon and bring them home.

passage.text: 👨‍🚀 Apollo 11 had 3 astronauts: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins. It launched on July 16, 1969.
🌕 On July 20, Armstrong and Aldrin landed in a small craft called the Eagle. Collins stayed behind, circling the Moon.
👣 Armstrong stepped out first. He said: "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind."
passage.q: Who stepped on the Moon first?

passage.text: 🌊 They splashed down in the ocean on July 24. Their footprints are still on the Moon. The Moon has no wind to blow them away!
passage.q: Why are the footprints still there?
passage.a: There is no wind on the Moon.

words: a person who travels in space
landing a spacecraft in the ocean
a big job with a goal
worksheet: The goal was set by President ______. Circle: Kennedy / Lincoln
First on the Moon: Circle: Armstrong / Aldrin / Collins
Collins stayed ______ the Moon. Circle: on / circling
The landing craft was called the ______. Circle: Eagle / Falcon
Footprints stay because the Moon has no ______. Circle: wind / rocks

Launch July 16, splashdown July 24. The trip took ____ days.
Challenge: On the Moon you weigh 1/6 as much. 72 lb on Earth = ____ lb
henry.challenge: On the Moon you weigh only 1/6 of your Earth weight. A 72 lb kid weighs how much there? (72 ÷ 6). Try your own weight too!

frankie.title: Footprints on the Moon 👣🌕
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud: Long ago, astronauts flew a rocket to the Moon. They walked and hopped there. Their footprints are still on the Moon! (About 14 minutes.)
steps: 👀 Look at the real Moon footprint photo.
🔤 Sound out h-o-p. Trace, then write it (stretch!).
links: Grown-up: show the bootprint. Say: this was made in 1969!
worksheet:
Fill the missing number. Circle it.
5   4   _   2   1   🚀
Circle: 3   6

Count the moons. Circle the number.
🌕🌕🌕 + 🌕🌕🌕 = 5   6   7

Sound it out. Draw a line to the picture.
hop   bug   bed
🐛   🛏️   🐇
Circle every on: I hop on the Moon. I am on the Moon.

Trace: I hop.
